analysis.title: Big Tech Hugs The Sierra Club, Gold Rips 3%: McElligott Decodes The "Glass Half-Full" Blue Tsunami Trade
key_insights: Emini S&P futures fell from about 7,630 to a low of 7,490 as the Democratic midterm wave grew, then rose almost 200 points to 7,687 after Trump said he could work with Democrats. That is a 2.6% round trip before the US open.

McElligott (Nomura) describes two layers behind the rebound. One is mechanical: tail hedges, especially puts, were monetized after the initial sell-off. The other is narrative: a Democratic Congress and statehouses are seen as a brake on AI capex, deficits, Iran and wealth taxes.

Client flow McElligott sees is 'constructive-not-wingy', mainly call spreads. They are the preferred year-end play on post-midterm seasonality and 'narrative moderation' after the recent degrossing purge.

Gold rose 2.9% to $4,053.60 by 7:27am ET and silver rose 4.7%. McElligott reads gold as pricing no tolerance for DOGE-like fiscal pain under a Democratic regime, plus a possible easing of selling from GCC countries and Iran if Trump's Iran resolve is weaker.

Last Friday's 3.7% gold plunge looked like a liquidity-raising move and took gold below fair value for the first time since 2023 (Bloomberg's Simon White). That left the metal washed out going into the vote.

The first and largest of McElligott's four rationalizations is that the election results force a moderation of US data center buildout. That would ease concerns about the hyperscaler capex 'prisoner's dilemma', credit and equity issuance, FCF burn, duration pressure and crowding-out risk to Treasuries.

Goldman's Privorotsky: Texas accounts for 26.7% of planned US data center capacity, and Hinojosa's market odds were 35% before the vote. She won. Goldman economists say states where Democrats are likely to restrict data centers hold roughly 45% of planned US capacity, and they expect short-term data center moratoria.
Goldman FX's Lightowler says Hinojosa will not lift the freeze until more comprehensive regulation passes, potentially pushing gigawatts due in 2027 into 2028.

McElligott notes Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Google are working with the Sierra Club, the League of Conservation Voters and the NRDC on a 'Responsible Data Center Development Collaborative'. His read is that this can move the buildout forward, just slower, and reduces the risk of a data center 'full stop'.

Debt issuance remains robust. Meta raised $15B in dollars on Tuesday, with orders as high as $58B, and is seeking up to EUR9B in its euro debut. An 11% discount on an Oracle offering signals buyer fatigue (Bloomberg ECM desk).

Third rationalization: Trump's 'no immediate plans' to strike Iran supports lower oil, lower yields and a lower dollar, which McElligott says is easing US financial conditions. WTI was down another 1.4%. WSJ reported the US struck Iran's Qeshm Island on Monday, and Iran's leader warned of a 'far wider' response.

Fourth rationalization: the 'swing hard-left to socialism' scare moderated. California voters rejected the billionaire wealth tax, and property tax increases met nationwide pushback. Massachusetts passed a millionaire tax and Michigan elected Abdul El-Sayed to the Senate.

BofA's Hartnett warned before the vote that a blue wave marks an electoral shift from populist capitalism to populist socialism, with stocks, the dollar and yields falling into year-end. Goldman's Cahill sides with McElligott, reading the vote as Republican revolt plus motivated Democrats rather than progressives outperforming.

McElligott sees only a modest net tailwind for lower rates and says rates can keep chopping around, with a touch of bias to lower yields. The 10Y was about 5bps lower near 4.915% before the 8:30am refunding announcement. Goldman's rates desk doubts Friday's payrolls can remove the hikes implied for the Fed.

The author argues only the hedge unwind is a mechanical flow and it runs out once puts are cashed. Nasdaq 100 futures erased earlier gains and turned negative just before 8am ET. The author suspects the glass is mostly hedges and that the AI debate resumes once the narrative bid fades.

sector_views.rationale: Democratic control of statehouses may slow data center buildout, with Texas and other states holding about 45% of planned capacity. Hyperscalers are collaborating on a national framework to avoid a full stop, but debt issuance remains heavy.

vol_and_positioning: Tail hedges, especially puts, were monetized after the initial 'Blue Tsunami' sell-off, which helped the futures rebound (McElligott).
Goldman's Privorotsky notes many hedges placed over recent days now need to be monetized.
Client flow is call spreads, the preferred year-end trade after the recent degrossing purge.
Once the puts are cashed there is no mechanical flow left to monetize, which is the author's reason for doubting the rally.
geopolitical: Trump said he has no immediate plans to launch strikes on Iran after the midterms.
WSJ reported the US attacked Iran's Qeshm Island on Monday as part of limited strikes carried out secretly in recent weeks.
Iran's leader warned that further attacks would bring a 'far wider' response (Bloomberg).
Speculated selling of gold by GCC countries and Iran may ease if US-Iran tensions fall.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers are collaborating on a national framework, so the buildout slows but does not stop. That eases financing, FCF burn and duration concerns (McElligott).
tension_points.bear_case: Goldman expects data center moratoria in states holding about 45% of planned capacity, and Texas's freeze could push 2027 gigawatts into 2028. Debt issuance is still heavy.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The hedge-unwind bid fading, after which the AI debate resumes, as the author argues. Also continued heavy debt issuance such as Meta's, which shows slower buildout has not reached bond markets.

tension_points.bull_case: McElligott and Goldman's Cahill read the vote as an anti-Trump referendum rather than a shift to socialism, citing California's rejection of the wealth tax.
tension_points.bear_case: Hartnett (BofA) warned a blue wave marks a shift to populist socialism, with stocks, the dollar and yields falling into year-end. Massachusetts passed a millionaire tax and Michigan elected El-Sayed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Friday's payrolls are unlikely to change the Fed pricing, per Goldman's rates desk. Further state-level tax measures passing would weaken the referendum read.
